description: Section-level URLs are well identified but the concrete recurring dataset files (XLSX/CSV) for cards, ATMs and POS terminals are not pinned down to exact URLs.

The NBUStatService OpenData API is confirmed to exist with directory and statistical-reporting endpoints, but the actual list of open-data blocks (and whether any covers card/ATM/POS series rather than only FX and reporting dimensions) was not enumerated.
No NBU statistical release calendar was located, so publication timing for card/terminal and cash series is inferred from observed cadence rather than documented.

Stable-URL publications (notably https://bank.gov.ua/files/stat.pdf) overwrite in place, and NBU has issued revised card-market figures, so historical and revision coverage is not guaranteed by URL harvesting alone.
The NBU maintains parallel uk and en editions, but whether the en edition lags or omits annexes was not tested.
Published aggregates give national totals; bank-level or acquirer-level ATM/POS breakdowns were not found in public releases.

Регіональні головні управління статистики (oblast statistics offices, e.g. cv./od./mk./kyiv.ukrstat.gov.ua) republish and sometimes extend household and retail-trade tables, but were only sampled, not enumerated.

Other non-NBU public bodies plausibly holding payment-relevant data were not searched in this pass: Держаудитслужба, Рахункова палата (audit of state banks and of cashless programmes), НКЦПФР, Держфінмоніторинг (cash transaction thresholds), and Укрпошта as a cash-distribution and payment agent in rural areas.

Public procurement (ProZorro / prozorro.gov.ua and its analytics layer bi.prozorro.org) was not searched, although it is the richest open channel for ATM and POS terminal tenders, quantities, models and prices.

English-language coverage of this cell is thin because these bodies publish primarily in Ukrainian; only the EU portal profile and the Держстат API page were found in English. No English-term equivalents were identified for РРО/ПРРО fiscalisation concepts, which have no clean English analogue.

Several search terms are noisy and degrade automated discovery: 'кешбек' overwhelmingly returns the National Cashback consumer programme rather than payment-market analysis; 'index.minfin.com.ua' is a private site easily mistaken for the Ministry of Finance; 'data.gov' searches in English drift to the US portal.

No regional or second-tier-bank-focused Ukrainian trade media were identified in this pass; all candidates are Kyiv-centric national outlets covering the large banks (PrivatBank, PUMB, Sense, Oschad) and national PSPs.

Only text media were assessed. Ukrainian fintech/banking podcasts, YouTube channels and conference video (including EMA and trade-outlet events) were not searched, yet executives often give the most specific unpublished numbers on stage or on camera.
Paywall/subscription status was only verified for Fintech Insider and Finclub; Forbes Ukraine, Mind.ua, NV and Interfax paywall tiers are assumed, not tested.

PSP/acquirer-side trade coverage is thinner than bank-side: NovaPay, iPay.ua, Portmone, LiqPay, Fondy, EasyPay and Concord-successor acquirers were only touched incidentally, and no PSP-specialist outlet was located.
No global newswire (Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, AFP, Dow Jones) confirmed as a tracked Ukraine payments channel in this pass.
Sanctions-and-payments coverage (scheme blockades, correspondent banking, cross-border restrictions affecting Ukraine) is represented only by a 2022 Finextra item.
Processing/acquiring and ATM-service vendors operating in Ukraine (e.g. Ukrainian Processing Center, acquirers, ATM deployers) have no confirmed recurring EN news channel.
EN coverage is Kyiv-centric; regional cash-access dynamics (frontline oblasts, de-occupied territories, POWER BANKING sites) are covered only anecdotally.
Pre-2022 English baseline coverage now sits largely in archive.kyivpost.com and defunct feeds, risking loss of the pre-war comparison series.
LinkedIn company-post and LinkedIn Jobs layer is unaddressed due to login gating and ToS.

Careers pages of several relevant actors were not individually located in this pass: Oschadbank, Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine, monobank/Universal Bank, Sense Bank, A-Bank, TAScombank, plus terminal/ATM vendors and integrators operating in UA (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Ingenico/PAX distributors, Printec-type integrators).
Conference agendas and speaker lists are ephemeral — organiser sites typically replace the previous edition's programme.
Conference presentation decks and video recordings — where the actual volume figures appear — were not located; only programmes and journalistic recaps were found.
Resume databases carry the strongest system-level disclosures but contain personal data.
Exact download URLs for the Реєстр платіжної інфраструктури, the non-bank registers search results, and the kis.bank.gov.ua backend were not obtained because bank.gov.ua rejects automated fetches.

Registers of currency-exchange operators, and any register of collection/cash-handling (інкасація) operators relevant to cash usage, were only partially touched via the legacy old.bank.gov.ua directory.
No systematic archive strategy identified for NBU register snapshots (only the DGF publishes a dated archive of its member list).
Cross-register joining (NBU licence lists vs ЄДР vs DGF vs aggregators) depends on consistent EDRPOU and MFO keys, which was not validated in this run.
Terms of use / API licensing for the commercial aggregators (YouControl, Opendatabot, Clarity Project) were not read in this run, so collection_allowed for them is a provisional assessment.

Only 3 of the ~9 NBU-licensed CIT operators were identified with a live web presence (CIT Security, Інкас Сервіс/cit.net.ua, Cash and Security). Українська сервісна інкасація, Перша інкасаторська компанія, О-МЕГА, Панорама Прикарпаття, Діамант Секʼюриті and Комсервіс-Безпека have no captured URLs.

Utility/biller side of cash bill payment is under-covered: regional oblenergo, gas (Нафтогаз/газозбут), water and heating utilities publish payment-collection (рівень розрахунків / оплата населення) statistics that implicitly reveal cash channel shares, and none were scouted in this pass.
Fuel networks (ОККО, WOG, Socar, БРСМ) and their cash mix, plus NovaPay/Нова пошта counter-based cash payments — a fast-growing non-bank cash acceptance channel — were not covered.

No source found that disaggregates cash usage by oblast or by frontline/de-occupied vs. rear regions, despite wartime cash demand being highly regional (power outages, damaged infrastructure, migration cited in Ukrposhta's own report).

Open-data and registry routes (data.gov.ua, Prozorro procurement of інкасація services by state bodies/banks, Opendatabot/YouControl) were not exercised; Prozorro tenders in particular would expose contracted cash-collection prices and volumes.
No verified CPV code list for ATM, POS/payment terminal, self-service kiosk, cash-processing and card-processing procurement in the Ukrainian classifier (ДК 021:2015).

Private commercial banks and non-bank PSPs (e.g. Raiffeisen, Universal/monobank, FUIB, PUMB, OTP, and independent ATM/terminal operators) are not subject to Prozorro and are largely absent from this cell's sources.
Contract-level documents (tender documentation, technical specifications, award protocols, signed contracts as attachments) were not individually assessed — only the portals that host them.
World Bank (UN Development Business / STEP), USAID and EU delegation procurement for Ukraine were not searched in this slice; only EBRD, UNDP/UNGM and TED were covered.

Several URLs (bipro.prozorro.org, dasu.gov.ua, prozorro.gov.ua/ProzorroMarket, tender.privatbank.ua) were recorded from search results and reasoning rather than fetched; access status and exact paths are unverified.

Smaller and niche banks (Банк Кредит Дніпро, ТАСкомбанк, Банк Восток, Правекс, Ідея Банк, Банк Львів, Юнекс, MTB, Полтава-банк) were not individually scouted; several are active card issuers or acquirer-adjacent.
Branch/ATM locator endpoints were identified conceptually (Kredobank, Pivdenny) but the underlying JSON/XHR feeds were not enumerated for any bank.
Foreign parent-group disclosures (RBI, BNP Paribas, OTP Group, Crédit Agricole, PKO BP for Kredobank) that carry Ukraine segment data were not scouted in this cell.
Interim (quarterly/half-year) bank reporting cadence and publication dates were not mapped, only annual artefacts.
POS terminal hardware OEM/distributor layer in Ukraine (Ingenico, PAX, Verifone, Castles, NEXGO channel partners) has no identified authoritative source.
Payment switch and HSM/key-management vendors and their Ukrainian integrators are not represented among candidates.
Quantitative vendor revenue and customer-concentration data sits behind registry-aggregator paywalls (YouControl, Opendatabot) rather than on free pages.
Vendor win announcements are frequently published only on LinkedIn or in conference materials rather than on corporate sites, and neither was systematically searched this run.
Several key references found are dated (Printec Ukraine 2019 management report, older AUB/Alfa-Bank processing-migration articles); current-year vendor activity is thinly covered.

E-money issuers (емітенти електронних грошей) and licensed wallet providers were not enumerated individually — only the NBU register that contains them was located. No named Ukrainian e-money/wallet operator with public volume data was captured this pass.
QR and instant account-to-account payment providers are uncovered at the operator level; no commercial provider was identified.
POS terminal estate and ATM fleet numbers were not obtained from any operator — only qualitative mobile-acquiring/SoftPOS narrative from Oschadbank and processing-scale claims from UPC.

Several candidate root URLs (liqpay.ua, fondy.io, portmone.com.ua, easypay.ua, ipay.ua, visa.com.ua, pumb press centre index) were inferred from search results and operator references rather than opened directly in this pass.
No archival strategy identified for operator KPI pages whose self-reported numbers change silently (RozetkaPay merchant counts, Solidgate client counts).
Cross-border/relocation-driven acquiring for Ukrainian merchants (Payoneer, Wise, Paysera, Unlimit, TransferGo) was only touched via the MTO query and not systematically mapped.

Acquirer/processor-side actors that sit between the schemes and merchants (e.g. UPC — Ukrainian Processing Center, Tas Link, and bank acquiring arms) were not searched in this pass; they publish terminal-fleet and acceptance data relevant to ATM/POS coverage.
Scheme operating rules and Ukraine-specific rule bulletins (Visa Core Rules regional annexes, Mastercard rules) were not located for Ukraine.
PROSTIR transaction-level statistics (volumes/values, not just active-card counts) were not located on prostir.gov.ua itself; only scheme-split card counts via NBU/press.
National Cashback / Дія-linked payment programmes involving Mastercard were mentioned in interviews but their official programme pages were not mapped.
Cross-border remittance corridors into Ukraine (scheme-based push-to-card, Visa Direct / Mastercard Move) and their NBU-reported volumes were not covered.
No association source found for cash-in-transit, cash-management or ATM-deployment in Ukraine, and ATMIA's Ukrainian membership (if any) was not confirmed.
Both AUB (which exposes an /avtoryzatsiia login) and ATMIA place an unknown share of their statistics behind member authentication. The public/gated boundary was not mapped.

The UAFIC fintech catalogue itself (PDF or interactive map, 2023/2024/2025 editions) was described in secondary reporting but its direct download URLs were not located, because the association site is JS-rendered.
EMA's member register was confirmed to exist and be rich (~80+ organisations) but is rendered as a logo gallery, so a machine-readable member list was not produced in this pass.

Only Kyiv-centric national associations were found; regional banking unions, chambers of commerce (Торгово-промислова палата України) and employer federations (Федерація роботодавців України) were not searched, and they often host banking/payments committees.
English-language association coverage was thinner than Ukrainian: only EBA, GB4U and ATMIA were reached in English, and no English-language mirror of NABU/AUB/EMA statistical output was confirmed.

Payment-scheme and network-adjacent commercial research (Visa/Mastercard commissioned consumer payment studies for Ukraine, and acquirer/processor white papers such as UPC or Ukrainian PSPs) was not searched in this pass.

No Russian-language (ru) searching was performed, although a meaningful share of legacy Ukrainian financial-analytics content (including rating agency archives such as standard-rating.biz/rus/) exists in Russian.
Several candidates (Fitch, Statista, Euromonitor, GlobalData) are behind registration or paywalls, and no candidate URL in this slice was fetched or liveness-checked.
Cash-usage-specific commercial research (cash-in-transit, ATM cash cycle, cash logistics vendors' market studies) is thinly covered; only demand-side survey material (Info Sapiens) addresses it.

Strategy consultancies beyond the Big Four (McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Roland Berger, Oliver Wyman) were referenced only indirectly via a secondary blog citation of McKinsey payments work; their Ukraine/CEE payments publications were not systematically searched.

It is not yet confirmed which POS-terminal series (POS terminals per 100,000 adults / per 1,000 km2, card transaction volumes) the NBU actually reports to IMF FAS for Ukraine, or how many years are populated.

Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB), Nordic institutions (NEFCO/NIB), KfW/DEG, JICA and the Ukraine Development Fund / Ukraine Facility structures were not searched in this pass despite being listed donor-platform members.

IFI procurement notices and award records (World Bank Procurement/STEP, EBRD ECEPP, EIB tenders) were not covered — these are the layer that names equipment, suppliers and contract values for ATM/POS and banking infrastructure.
Ukrainian-language coverage in this cell rests mainly on MoF, NBU, mindev and NISS pages; IFI-side uk-language content (EIB ?lang=uk pages, IMF /uk section) was only lightly sampled.
Findex is triennial and FAS annual with long lags; neither captures wartime year-on-year shifts in Ukrainian cash usage and POS deployment.
